text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Britain's envoy on the Cyprus problem David Hannay is feeling the ground for the possibility of a rotating presidency between the two sides.
- An international campaign is to start to condemn Turkey after the killing of a retired fireman on Sunday.
- Civil servants union asks government to repeal a decision to privatise postal services.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Security Council members condemn the killing of Petros Kakoulis, buried yesterday.
- British bases on Cyprus are put in the spotlight over live fire exercises in the Akamas area.
- The government is to lodge a formal protest over Sunday's killing to the United Nations next week.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Hold your buns. Big Mac (McDonalds) is coming to Cyprus.
- Tetra Pak is to close its Cyprus offshore activities and relocate in Egypt.
- Interamerican Insurance profits rise in H1.
- Economic growth is to reach 3.5 percent in 1997.
HARAVGHI
- David Hannay is discussing the possibility of changing the constitutional system of government to include rotating presidency.
- New bomb goes off in Limassol.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Experts decide not to construct a marina at Paralimni, and propose changes to plans for marina development elsewhere.
- Cyprus would crumble if an earthquake took place with an epicentre in the centre of the island, says a Greek seismologist.
SIMERINI
- Students stage protests at the Ledra Palace checkpoint over the killing of Petros Kakoulis.

- The Democratic Party and the Democratic Rally have agreed to change the electoral law to reinforced proportional representation from simple proportional representation for forthcoming municipal elections.
